newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index ends up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index ends up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Wednesday thanks to an absense of fresh negative news hitting the market but trading was slow and choppy, indicating that investors remain cautious, traders said.
The B index closed up 0.869 points or 1.01 percent at 86.632 points on volume of 12.4 million shares worth $9.8 million, compared with $11.711 million on Tuesday.

The failure so far of rumours predicting new government crackdown measures to be borne out encouraged institutional buying on Wednesday, brokers said. But retail investors were cautious to follow up in light of the recent volatility.
"Institutional buying supported the market today," said one broker. "But volume has not picked up, indicating sentiment is still cautions and the potential for further rises is limited."
Of 43 B shares, 32 traded, with 20 up, two flat and 10 down.
Shanghai Steel Tube Co 900926.SS was the star on speculative buying, jumping $0.012 or 7.69 percent to $0.168 on volume of 20,000 shares.

Blue-chip Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Co was the most actively traded and became the third winner on institutional window-dressing buying, rising $0.042 or 4.66 percent to $0.942 on volume of 1.7 million shares.
Market barometer, Shanghai Lujiazui Finance Trade Zone Development Co, was the second most actively traded on institutional buying, which gave the market some support, brokers said.
The stock ended up $0.020 or 1.39 percent to $1.450 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index dipped on weak sentiment due to the recent crackdown, brokers said.
It fell 12.615 points or 0.94 percent to 1,326.035 points on volume of 449.7 million shares worth 7.0 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index shed 28.850 points or 0.73 percent to 3,939.655 points.
Shanghai No 9 Department was the biggest loser on its ex-rights day today, slipping 0.58 yuan or 6.53 percent to 8.30 yuan on volume of 619,500 shares.
